protections: State persistence containment: a caller-supplied name reaching ConsciousnessExplorer.exportState (write) or importState (read) must resolve to a regular file directly inside a fixed per-feature state directory, with no separators, no parent segments, no symlinked final component and no non-regular target, decided in the library sink rather than in the MCP handler or the JSON inputSchema.

Vector file containment: the same rule for the separate solver MCP server's saveVectorToFile file_path (write, including the recursive directory creation the writer performs) and solveTrueSublinear vector_file (read), decided in a shared helper reached by both.

traps.reason_to_dismiss: The report and the advisory name the export_state write; import_state only reads a file whose path the caller already chose, applies it to in-memory state and never returns the file contents, so it looks like a read the client was already allowed to make.

saveVectorToFile and vector_file are numerical plumbing in the solver's own stdio MCP server (a different program from the consciousness-explorer server the advisory names); the advisory never mentions vectors, and the paths are supplied by the same MCP client that already supplies the matrix, so this reads as an unrelated feature.

Only the write at src/mcp/server.ts:1275 can clobber an existing file; mkdirSync with recursive:true merely creates directories, so a containment check inserted immediately before the write is enough and the directory creation above it can stay.

The state and vector directories are owned by the process, so an attacker cannot plant a symlink, a fifo or a device node inside them; rejecting separators and parent segments in the name is therefore sufficient, and a plain writeFileSync/readFileSync needs no flags.

The inputSchema is the tool's declared contract and every caller of the tool goes through the MCP request handler, so a pattern on filepath/file_path (or a path check inside handleExportState / handleSaveVectorToFile) is the natural and sufficient place to enforce the rule.
The path comes from an operator typing the CLI command, not from a caller of the MCP server, so it is not attacker-controlled and the advisory's MCP-tool threat model does not cover it.

No code in the repository calls ProofLogger.exportProof and ProofLogger is not re-exported from the package entry point (src/consciousness-explorer/index.js:10-37), so it reads as an internal proof/debug helper rather than an exposed route; the class already writes its normal reports into its configured logDir.

These are operator-owned --output flags on the local command line in the main solver CLI (a different tree from the landing point); the advisory's file arguments are MCP tool arguments, not CLI flags.
This is a third sub-package's operator CLI, far from the advisory, and the only in-repo caller of exportMetrics passes a timestamped /tmp path, so no attacker controls these paths.
dist/ is generated output; npm run build (clean + tsc) regenerates it from src/mcp/server.ts, so it needs no fix of its own.

The natural fix is a plain basename inside a fixed state directory, and the CLI's arbitrary-path behaviour is not a security contract, so it is acceptable for export/import/evolve --export to start rejecting absolute paths and for the in-repo example to be updated; a security rule should win over convenience.

vector_file and file_path are internal solver plumbing whose only documented workflow is the generateTestVector + saveVectorToFile round trip, so moving the files under a fixed package data directory and refusing caller-chosen paths is harmless.

masking.what: A pattern on the export_state inputSchema or a check in handleExportState makes the tool look fixed while import_state (server.js:545-546), the library method and every non-MCP producer of the same sink stay unguarded.

A name-only basename check makes traversal look closed, but a symlink planted as the final component of the permitted name is still followed by plain writeFileSync/readFileSync (index.js:288, server.ts:1275, server.ts:1184) until O_NOFOLLOW and a regular-file check are added.

Fixing only src/mcp/server.ts leaves the committed dist/mcp/server.js copy (1041, 1121) exploitable; the fix only becomes effective for consumers of the published package after npm run build regenerates dist (package.json:39-44).

Adopting a strict basename rule to close the sink makes the CLI and the repository's own example fail, which can look like a regression to the solver and push them back to a weaker handler-only check.

conflicts.what: T6 says the decision must live in the library sink so non-MCP producers are covered, but T12 says that same library must keep accepting the absolute paths the CLI (bin/cli.js:81, 361, 380) and the in-repo example (examples/psycho-symbolic-integration-test.js:122-123) pass to exportState/importState; a bare basename rule satisfies T6 and breaks T12, so the fix needs a trusted channel or an allowed-root rule rather than a name-only check.

Containment for vector_file/file_path must not break the documented generateTestVector + saveVectorToFile round trip: the tool description recommends it (server.ts:265), the response echoes the raw file_path (server.ts:1148) and derives format_used from it (server.ts:1150), and loadVectorFromFile resolves absolute paths (server.ts:1176); a helper that rewrites the path without echoing the resolved path breaks the workflow.

Hardening the name shape by refusing unknown extensions or leading dots conflicts with saveVectorToFile defaulting to JSON for a name with no known extension (server.ts:1289-1290) and with legitimate dotfile state names; the shape rule must reject separators/traversal and non-regular targets, not punctuation.

fairness_risks: The MCP tool schemas advertise an arbitrary path ('Path to save state file' at src/consciousness-explorer/mcp/server.js:246 and :260; 'Output file path' at src/mcp/server.ts:368). A basename-in-a-fixed-directory rule changes the published tool contract, so the task must state which absolute paths become illegal before a solver can be scored on refusing them.

The consciousness-explorer CLI documents export <filepath>, import <filepath> and evolve --export <path> with arbitrary paths (README.md:132, :173, :217, :220; cli.js:46, :98, :353, :373) and its own integration example calls exportState('/tmp/consciousness-state-test.json') (examples/psycho-symbolic-integration-test.js:122-123). Any containment rule in the library sink breaks these unless the CLI/example get a trusted mode or are rewritten, so an over-broad fix is rewarded by security tests and punished by every other use in the repo.

loadVectorFromFile resolves absolute paths by design (src/mcp/server.ts:1176) and the repository keeps large vectors as data files (tests/data/test-vector.json, tests/large_vector_10000.json); a rule that refuses absolute or subdirectory-containing paths rejects the repository's own solver workflow.

ProofLogger.exportProof exists to write proof data to a caller-chosen path 'for external verification' (proof-logger.js:645-646); a containment rule defeats its documented purpose, so if it is scored it needs a trusted option rather than a hard basename rule.

saveVectorToFile defaults the format to JSON when the name has no known extension (server.ts:1289-1290), and a legitimate state name may start with a dot; refusing those shapes as suspicious rejects legitimate inputs.

The advisory text quoted here names only export_state; scoring a solver on the operator CLI routes (T7, T9, T10) makes it responsible for code the published fix never touched and that has no untrusted caller, which the task's own O8 entries dismiss as not attacker-controlled.

design.why: Two fix families carry five independent judgements, each with a different reason to dismiss. T2: the read direction is not the write the advisory names, yet import_state reaches the same feature and can disclose file content through the JSON.parse error text returned at server.js:317-321 (deepseek-type). T3: a second MCP server in the same npm package exposes saveVectorToFile and vector_file with the identical exposure, in a numerical feature the report never mentions (deepseek-type). T6: the check must live in the shared sink because the inputSchema is only metadata, the handler forwards raw args (server.js:270-272), and the CLI and the example reach the same sink (deepseek-type, the candidate's j_tempting_wrong_fix). T5: name containment alone is not enough - O_NOFOLLOW and a regular-file check are needed for the final component, or a symlink/device node defeats a perfect basename check (mimo-type how mechanism). T12: the strict basename rule that closes the sink breaks the CLI's documented absolute paths and the repository's own /tmp example, so the solver must choose a design that keeps a trusted channel (mimo-type coupled value). This beats a design built on T1 alone (trivial, the report describes it) and beats a design built on the uncovered CLI routes T7-T10, which are operator-trusted, were not touched by the published fix, and would need harness-authored tests outside the advisory. T3 is backed by a second published fix commit, so the vector family is known to be in scope for this advisory; T5 and T12 are the decisions that separate a plausible wrong fix from the published one. T11 is free once the vector helper is fixed and the project is rebuilt.

unverified: The fix commits a701296e363192be863e79d788fa268095e3d229 and ea9a212b69e4449ec443fe088a7aec7546f70b4a and the screener's fix.diff were not present in the worktree and no shell was available, so the exact published implementation (resolveStatePath/resolveVectorPath, O_NOFOLLOW, the fixed directory location) is taken from the screener record, not read from code.
Whether the published fix actually rejects the CLI/example absolute paths (T12) is unknown; the pinned code is pre-fix, and the screener records an over-broad-fix penalty rather than the diff.
Whether the grading harness runs npm run build before hidden tests is unknown; if tests import the committed dist/mcp/server.js without rebuilding, T11 is a real failure mode for a src-only fix.

Whether the MCP SDK version in use validates a tool's inputSchema server-side was not verified (node_modules absent); the server handler demonstrably does not validate args against the schema (server.js:270-272), which is the evidence T6 relies on.

The read-direction disclosure path for T2/T3 relies on Node's JSON.parse error text including a short snippet of the parsed content; the exact V8/Node behaviour and snippet length were reasoned from Node 20+ behaviour but not executed.
No H3 history could be inspected: shell was disabled, so no earlier security fix in the repository history was examined; the history fields are null rather than false.

Repo size, build and test execution were not measured or run (shell disabled); whether npm run build and node --test tests/ succeed at the pinned commit is untested. The project has no test that mentions export_state, import_state, saveVectorToFile or vector_file (grep over tests/ returned no match).

The M5-style config paths (emergence/persistent-learning-system.ts:366-376 via emergence/index.ts:77, breakthrough-session-logger.js:521-530 via a saveLocation option, proof-logger.js:17 logDir) were not traced to any MCP request argument; no MCP file-path tool exists in the neural-pattern-recognition server (src/neural-pattern-recognition/src/server.js has no fs import), so they were not recorded as traps.

The neural-pattern-recognition monitoring exportMetrics has exactly one in-repo caller that passes a timestamped /tmp path (production-integration.js:551-552); whether external consumers call it with caller-controlled paths is unknown.
